text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Manchester City and Tottenham at the Etihad Stadium!
City have the chance to close the gap at the top of the league back to one point with a win here after Arsenal's victory over Wolves yesterday.

The Citizens are unbeaten in eight matches in all competitions (W6 D2), but have drawn their last two Premier League games, dropping leads against both Chelsea and Liverpool, with the latter bringing an end to their 23-game winning run at the Etihad.
They come into today on the back of a win though, coming from 2-0 down to beat RB Leipzig 3-2 and claim top spot in their Champions League group.
Spurs were flying high after 10 matchdays, sitting top of the table after a stellar unbeaten start to the season.
Since then, they've lost three on the bounce, taking the lead in all of those matches only to come away with no points.
It's a run that's seen them drop to sixth in the table, but a win here would move them level on points with today's opponents.
Spurs have the best winning record against Pep Guardiola's City, winning six of their meetings, however, only one of those victories has come at the Etihad - a 3-2 win in February 2022.
Guardiola makes three changes to the side that came back to win against Leipzig on Tuesday.
Ederson is back in goal, with Doku and Alvarez coming in to join the front line.
Ortega, Lewis and Grealish drop to the bench, where Stones and Kovacic are also named after recovering from injury.
Ange Postecoglou makes just one change from their loss to Aston Villa last weekend, and it's an enforced one.
Bentancur picked up an ankle injury in that game, so he's out, but Bissouma is back from suspension to replace him.
They're still without a recognised centre-back, as Emerson and Davies are paired up again.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Silva gets the game under way for City!
City are enjoying all of the early possession here, and Doku manages to find space down the left to drive into.
He's looking to pull it back to Alvarez, but Porro's interception takes it out for a corner.
Ederson comes out of his box to help City start playing it out from the back, but he's quickly chased down by Son.
The keeper clears his lines in time, and the hosts do well to pass their way through the high press.
GOOD SAVE! Doku is already causing problems down the left side, and he gets the better of Porro to drill a low shot at Vicario's near post.
The keeper gets down to smother it.
SON SCORES! From a City corner, Spurs break upfield at lightning-quick speed.
Kulusevski plays an early throughball around the back of Doku, who didn't realise that Son was behind him.
The Spurs captain holds off the Belgian to take it into the box before firing his shot through Ederson and into the back of the net.
1-0 Spurs!
It's a wonderful throughball from Kulusevski to cut the lines wide open for Spurs, and it caused a lot of confusion for Doku, who thought he had it covered.
City don't want to be behind for long and they quickly work it upfield before Silva wins a free-kick on the right after he's clipped by Lo Celso.
OWN GOAL! How quickly things can change! It's a brilliant whipped delivery from Alvarez on the free-kick and Haaland gets the deftest of flicks on it at the front of the crowd.
Emerson swings a leg at it and misses, and Son is behind him.
It bounces off the captain's thigh and into the back of the net before Vicario can react.
It's been a rollercoaster of a game for Son already, and there's only 11 minutes on the clock.
He's bearing down on Ederson, trying to rush the keeper into making a mistake, but again the Brazilian coolly clears his lines.
SAVE! Spurs are all over the place at the back as City just up the pace once more.
Foden cuts inside from the right before taking aim, and Emerson swings out a leg to block it.
It bounces to Silva, and Vicario smothers his shot from a tight angle.
WHAT A MISS! Spurs are caught in possession deep in their own half, and Silva quickly squares it into Haaland, who is unmarked in the middle.
He takes on the shot first-time, dragging it just wide of the far post to everybody's disbelief.
Gvardiol gets in on the action by carrying the ball a long way down the left before curling in his cross.
Haaland is a little sloppy with his first touch so he can't get a shot away, but he does manage to keep the attack alive.
BLOCK! Spurs just can't clear their lines at the moment, and Lo Celso gets caught on the ball on the edge of the D.
Silva doesn't have space to shoot so dinks it into Haaland, and his shot is blocked by Bissouma.
After soaking up another spell of City pressure, Spurs are patiently trying to play out from the back.
Up against the hosts' high press, they're struggling though, and they can't get over the halfway line.
Porro's cross is headed into the ground by Haaland, and that allows Gil to keep it alive.
He touches it onto Johnson, who quickly wins another Spurs corner, but this one is cleared by Akanji.
CHANCE! Lo Celso sweeps it out to Johnson on the right, and he bursts past Gvardiol to get into the box before drilling in a low cross.
He's looking for Son in the middle, but Dias slides in to deflect it just wide of the near post.
Son's goal was his 50th on the road in the Premier League.
He's only the second Spurs player to score 50+ away goals in the competition for the club after Harry Kane (scored 112).
City get caught playing out from the back once more as Silva plays a loose pass into Dias.
Gil pounces on it, and Spurs get a corner from it as Silva holds his hand up in apology.
OFF THE BAR! Doku has been a bright spark for City since the first whistle, and he makes another bursting run down the left.
When he's lost Porro, he cuts inside, firing a powerful shot over Vicario that rattles the underside of the bar before bouncing out off the inside of the far post.
FODEN SCORES! City have turned this game around! It's a wonderful team goal that starts with Emerson's sloppy clearance.
City knock it around Spurs with a series of one-touch passes, and it's worked through Haaland, Doku and Alvarez before it comes to Foden.
He has time to take a touch before firing it past Vicario at his near post.
2-1 City!
Alvarez was afforded too much space down the left of City's box, and he doesn't even need to glance up, knowing Foden is following in to the near post.
BLOCK! Doku is left in a pile on the floor, but the referee plays the advantage to City as Foden comes away with it.
He fizzes a dangerous low cross into the six-yard box, and Davies slides in to block it ahead of Alvarez.
It's a late one from Rodri on Porro as he slides in, getting none of the ball.
He's not happy to see he's getting a yellow card though.
OFF THE POST! Spurs are caught in possession again, and Akanji slides it forward for Alvarez.
After seeing no support, he chooses to go it alone, and his skidding low shot skims the far post.
MISS! Haaland misses another great chance! Silva trips in the box, but he still manages to stretch past Davies to tee up Haaland.
He rushes the shot knowing that Davies is sliding in, and he blazes it high over the bar into the stands.
Udogie gets nowhere near the ball as he clips the back of Foden's heels to take him out.
He goes into the referee's book.
It's poor defending from Spurs, who are choosing to sit back instead of closing down City's attacking players.
They give Doku too much room to pick out another cross, but luckily, Foden can't pick out a team-mate when he recycles it.
Porro drops off as Doku pushes forward once more, but he hits this cross against Emerson's shins.
Rodri follows in to keep it alive, only to trip over the ball on the edge of the box.
All of City's attacks are coming down the left at the moment as Doku cuts inside once more.
He drills another low cross into the box just as the offside flag goes up against him.
Into the first of three added minutes here and Spurs are enjoying a spell of possession in their own half.
Vicario eventually decides to go long, but Johnson can't keep hold of it under pressure from Dias.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-1 TOTTENHAM.
City come from behind to take a 2-1 lead over Spurs into half-time.
The visitors couldn't have made a better start, with Son scoring with their first shot of the game following a quick counter-attack.
He got the better of Doku before firing through Ederson.
Things quickly flipped on their head for the Spurs captain though, as his own goal just three minutes later pulled City level.
Doku then fired a powerful shot that bounced off the bar and post before being cleared.
Foden put them in front by finishing off a fine team move before Alvarez also struck the foot of the post.
It's a familiar story for Postecoglou as his side took the lead only to find themselves behind.
They still have time to fix things here, but they're going to need a much-improved performance in all areas of the pitch.
Guardiola will be pleased with how his side reacted, but they could have more goals given the number of chances they created - he'll want to see them be much more clinical after the break.
There's a change at the break for Spurs.
Gil, who has struggled to make an impact in this game, goes off for Hojbjerg.
Spurs get us back under way for the second half!
GREAT SAVE! Just 18 seconds into the second half and Vicario has to tip it wide.
Haaland cushions it into Silva, who hits the shot first-time with the outside of his boot.
It's swerving towards the far corner, but the keeper dives to deny him.
Spurs really need to cut out these mistakes, especially so close to their own goal.
Hojbjerg gives the ball away to Silva, but luckily for the midfielder, three defenders get in the way of the strike.
Hojbjerg can't get tight enough to Haaland, and City have another free-kick in a good position through the middle.
Alvarez clips it into the box, but it's comfortably cleared by Davies.
City are making their first change of the game now.
Doku hasn't been as bright since the start of the second half and appears to be limping as he goes off for Grealish.
SAVE! Johnson has switched out to the left since Gil went off, and he cuts inside to lose Walker before drilling a low shot on goal.
It's comfortably saved by Ederson.
Another sloppy pass in midfield sets Grealish away down the left and he clips a pacy cross into the far post.
It's just behind Haaland, who awkwardly stretches to reach it, but he can't direct it on target.
Udogie is making good progress down the left when he's penalised for a foul on Foden.
The Spurs players aren't happy that it's gone against them and the referee has to get involved to calm some tempers.
There were just 137 seconds between Son putting Spurs 1-0 up and then scoring an own goal in the first half.
He's only the second player in Premier League history to score a goal and an own goal in the opening 10 minutes of a game, after Gareth Barry for Aston Villa v Charlton in May 1999.
Grealish slightly moves his arm to block a throughball, and though he's protesting his innocence, he's still shown a yellow card.
It's a costly one too, as he'll miss the game against his old club Aston Villa on Wednesday.
SAVE! Spurs switch it out to Lo Celso on the left, and he instantly slides it forward for Udogie to chase.
He cuts inside before trying to poke it to Son, who has an empty net to aim for.
Ederson smothers it just as the offside flag goes up.
There's another nervy moment at the back for Spurs as Bissouma touches it back to Vicario, with Silva hovering in the box.
The keeper hurries his clearance, but luckily, Davies manages to slice it to safety.
Spurs have actually seen more of the ball in the second half, having 61 per cent of the possession so far, but they can't seem to do anything with it.
Bissouma does manage to win a corner, but Lo Celso curls it straight into Ederson's gloves.
LO CELSO EQUALISES! It's City caught on the ball this time, as Davies cuts out a throughball to Haaland, and his header picks out Son through the middle.
He lays it off to Lo Celso, who checks back before curling his shot towards the near post from the edge of the D.

source.text: He lays it off to Lo Celso

text: Ederson gets fingertips to it, but can only help it onto the post and in.
There was space ahead of Son if he'd wanted to take on a shot himself, but he unselfishly chose to lay it off to Lo Celso instead.
BLOCK! Porro's corner misses everyone in the middle but skims through to Lo Celso on the edge of the box.
He lets it bounce before putting his laces through it, and a deflection off Dias takes it wide.
Guardiola is making a change to try and shift the momentum back in his team's favour.
The scorer of the second goal, Foden, is taken off for Lewis.
Porro gets too tight to Grealish, taking his legs out from behind.
He's the second Spurs player into the book.
WIDE! It's better from City here as they start to move it with pace once more.
Lewis darts in behind, taking it to the byline before pulling it back for Rodri.
He hits the shot first time, but it swerves just wide of the top corner.
Lo Celso has scored in back-to-back Premier League games, this after only scoring in one of his first 58 appearances in the competition beforehand.
Two of his three goals in the competition have come against City (also November 2020).
Lo Celso's game is now over as he's replaced by Skipp.
GREALISH SCORES! City are back in front! It stems from a loose touch by Bissouma in midfield and Rodri latches onto it before threading it forward for Haaland down the right.
He squares it into the middle, putting it on a plate for Grealish to guide into the back of the net.
3-2 City!
Haaland's touch in front of goal might not be as good as usual today, but his assist for Grealish is perfectly weighted, and the substitute doesn't have to break stride.
Spurs get it moving quickly from the restart, and they still have the belief they can get something from this game.
They're pushing bodies forward, but can't get it into the box at the moment.
Gvardiol slides in and catches Skipp, who had his foot raised to cushion the ball, with a high boot.
The defender gives a shake of his head as he's shown a yellow card.
Kulusevski skips his way down the right, only to fire his cross straight against Lewis.
The resulting corner is taken short, but this time, it's Lewis that comes out on top as his tackle earns a goal-kick.
There are changes for both sides now, starting with a double one for City.
Gvardiol, who is on a booking, makes way for Ake.
And Kovacic comes on to help see out the three points in place of Alvarez.
For Spurs, it's Bissouma that's taken off, with an added goal threat in Richarlison on in his place.
Spurs are still trying to push for a late equaliser, but they just can't keep hold of the ball at the moment.
As soon as they cross into City's half, they get sloppy, and Rodri comes away with it this time.
KULUSEVSKI EQUALISES! There was nothing sloppy about that! Skipp pushes his way past two in midfield before Son helps it out to Johnson on the left side.
He has nobody marking him and clips a good cross towards the penalty spot, where Kulusevski rises above Ake to get his head on it and loop his effort into the back of the net.
There was no urgency for Walker to get tight to Johnson, who was able to get his head up and pick out the perfect cross.
Kulusevski is desperate to protect the draw he's just given to his side.
He's late tackling Grealish though, and gives away a free-kick as well as picking up a booking.
The referee pulls the game back for a foul on Haaland, not realising that he could've played the advantage with Grealish on the ball.
City players surround him, and they're screaming their protests at him, not that it'll change anything now.
Emerson rushes off his goal line to get involved in the protests against that decision from the referee and he's booked for dissent.
Haaland was screaming in the referee's face to say that he should've let play carry on.
He can't really have any complaints about the yellow card after what he did, but it only enrages him further.
Spurs' final roll of the dice sees Donley come on to make his debut for the club in place of Johnson.
It's a lovely floated cross into the far post by Rodri and Akanji goes down in the box under pressure from Skipp.
The midfielder had his arm over his shoulder, but there was nothing in it.
No penalty is given, which only frustrates City further.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 3-3 TOTTENHAM.
Spurs come from behind twice to snatch a late point in a 3-3 draw against City.
The visitors took the lead six minutes in with their first shot as Son finished off a counter-attack, but the Spurs captain then scored an own goal three minutes later to level things up.
Foden gave City the lead for the first time just after the half-hour mark, finishing off a flowing team move.
Doku and Alvarez also struck the woodwork.
Lo Celso got his side back into it, curling in a delightful shot that Ederson couldn't keep out.
Grealish tapped City in front once more, but Spurs weren't finished as Kulusevski looped in a headed equaliser in the 90th minute.
Tempers flared late on as City were denied the advantage when Grealish was in on goal, but in the end, neither team could find a winner.
For the first time since Guardiola's first season in charge, City draw three games in a row in the Premier League and it leaves them third in the table.
They travel to Villa on Wednesday.
Spurs' losing run comes to an end, but they stay fifth.
They host West Ham on Thursday.
That's all for today, goodbye!
